title: performance canary: adaptive hysteresis + KV-aware thresholds for rollout guards
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds adaptive hysteresis to performance canary detector, introduces KV-aware thresholding, and tightens automated rollback guards to reduce false positives while improving sensitivity to real regressions.
description: Context: Recent incidents highlighted two recurring problems with our perf canary rollouts: (1) sensitivity to transient p95 spikes during load variance that triggered unnecessary rollbacks, and (2) missed regressions when KV-cache hit ratios skewed latency/throughput signals. This PR implements an adaptive hysteresis algorithm and KV-aware thresholds to make rollout guards both more robust and more sensitive to real regressions.  What this changes (summary): - Adaptive hysteresis: replace fixed hold/release windows with a percentile-driven window that expands/contracts based on recent signal noise. Uses rolling 5m/30m percentiles to decide enter/exit conditions. - KV-aware thresholds: separate latency/throughput baselines for requests with KV-cache hits vs misses; canary detector now tags samples and applies the appropriate baseline. - Per-route sensitivity tuning: allow routes to opt into conservative or aggressive modes via canary policy. - Rollout guard tightening: automated rollback if sustained (10m) p95 latency regression >12% or throughput drop >8% when controlling for KV-hit normalized traffic; added hysteresis to prevent oscillation. - Observability: new metrics (canary.hysteresis_window_ms, canary.kv_hit_ratio, canary.kv_normalized_p95_ratio) and dashboards for A/B comparisons. - Tests and tooling: unit tests for new detector logic, integration tests in perf-canary harness, and a small canary simulation harness to reproduce edge cases from incidents. Commits (high-level): - feat(canary): adaptive hysteresis algorithm + docs - feat(canary): KV-aware baseline computation and tagging - refactor(canary): extract signal windowing utilities - test(canary): add unit + integration tests and simulation harness - infra(ci): increase flakiness timeout for perf tests; add perf-canary simulation job Files changed (high level): - internal/canary/detector.go (core algorithm + tests) - internal/canary/policy.go (per-route sensitivity) - internal/canary/kv_baselines.go (baseline computation + caching) - observability/dashboards/canary_overview.json - perf-canary/harness/simulator.go - perf-canary/tests/integration_canary_test.go - go.mod / go.sum updates for new dependencies (hdrhistogram, go-metrics) Why this design: Adaptive hysteresis reduces noisy rollbacks by expanding the exit window when variance increases, while still allowing quick rollbacks when the signal is clear. KV-aware baselines address a class of false negatives where cached traffic masks backend regressions; by normalizing signals we surface regressions that affect cold-paths and backend throughput. CI and validation: First CI run failed on an intermittent perf test (integration_canary_test.go) due to a race in the simulator; I fixed the simulator timing edge and re-ran CI. Final CI: all unit, integration, and lint checks passed; a separate perf-job run on our canary cluster was executed in the staging org and produced expected canary metrics (p95/p99 trajectories before/after). Review notes: - Carlos: suggested tightening the default rollback thresholds; I lowered the default throughput rollback from 10% to 8% and added per-route override. - Ruth: asked for metrics names consistency with dashboards; updated metric names and dashboard panels. - Benji: requested additional unit tests covering the percentile expansion behavior; added three focused tests. - Marta: requested a short migration note for existing canary policies; added migration guidance in docs/canary-migration.md. Merge: squashed and merged to main after approvals. Rollout: deployed to staging canary cluster first, observed expected behavior, then scheduled gradual rollout to prod canaries the following day. Related: ENG-8421 (adaptive hysteresis epic), SUP-9012 (incident follow-up).
